I have implemented the requested change to display failed CONNECT requests in `mitmdump`.

### Changes Made

1. **Handle `http_connect_error` in [`Dumper`](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/mitmproxy/addons/dumper.py#L48)**:
   - Added [`http_connect_error`](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/mitmproxy/addons/dumper.py#L297-L298) in [mitmproxy/addons/dumper.py](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/mitmproxy/addons/dumper.py) which delegates to `self.error(f)`.

2. **Added Unit Test**:
   - Added [`test_http_connect_error`](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/test/mitmproxy/addons/test_dumper.py#L330-L347) in [test/mitmproxy/addons/test_dumper.py](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/test/mitmproxy/addons/test_dumper.py) verifying that failed CONNECT flows are properly formatted and printed based on `flow_detail`.

### Why

`mitmdump` relies on the [`Dumper`](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/mitmproxy/addons/dumper.py#L48) addon to print flows to output. When an HTTP CONNECT request fails (for instance, when the upstream server is unreachable or requires authentication), the HTTP stream layer triggers the [`HttpConnectErrorHook`](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/_hooks.py#L115) (invoking `http_connect_error`) rather than standard `response` or `error` hooks. Because [`Dumper`](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/mitmproxy/addons/dumper.py#L48) did not implement an `http_connect_error` handler, failed CONNECT requests produced no output in `mitmdump`. By routing `http_connect_error` to [`error`](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/mitmproxy/addons/dumper.py#L293-L295), failed CONNECT flows are now dumped consistently like other failed HTTP flows.
